HomeIsolation — extension of existing `IsolationLayers`\n352\t\n353\t### Existing primitive (read-only — cite for reuse)\n354\t\n355\t`src/superclaude/cli/sprint/executor.py:107-182` `IsolationLayers` already implements 4-layer per-subprocess isolation:\n356\t\n357\t| Layer | Env var | Purpose |\n358\t|---|---|---|\n359\t| Working directory | `CLAUDE_WORK_DIR` | Per-task cwd |\n360\t| Git ceiling | `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` | Prevents accidental parent-repo writes |\n361\t| Plugin dir | `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DIR` | Isolates plugin discovery |\n362\t| Settings dir | `CLAUDE_SETTINGS_DIR` | Isolates `settings.json` per subprocess |\n363\t\n364\t### What we add (new — `cli/eval/isolation.py`)\n365\t\n366\t`HomeIsolation` subclasses or composes `IsolationLayers` and adds:\n367\t\n368\t| Layer | Env var | Purpose |\n369\t|---|---|---|\n370\t| **HOME** | `HOME` (and `XDG_*` overrides) | Per-eval `~/.claude/` — full hook+state+log isolation |\n371\t| **Session ID stamp** | `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` | Deterministic session_id for assertion lookups (eval-id-derived) |\n372\t| **Time offset** | `CLAUDE_FAKE_TIME_OFFSET` | Optional; lets evals advance the clock for 30-min freshness tests (E3) |\n373\t\n374\t### Interface signature (not implementation)\n375\t\n376\t```python\n377\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n378\tclass HomeIsolation:\n379\t    eval_id: str                   # e.g., \"E1\" or \"E2.1\"\n380\t    home_root: Path                # /tmp/eval-runs/<run>/E1/home\n381\t    session_id: str                # deterministic: hash(eval_id + run_id)[:16]\n382\t    time_offset_sec: int = 0\n383\t\n384\t    def setup(self) -> None:\n385\t        \"\"\"Create HOME/.claude/{hooks,state,logs}; deploy 9 freshness scripts;\n386\t        write settings.json; seed state files per manifest.\"\"\"\n387\t\n388\t    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:\n389\t        \"\"\"Return env-var overlay for the subprocess: HOME, XDG_*, CLAUDE_*,\n390\t        plus pass-through of PATH, USER, TERM, LANG, CI.\"\"\"\n391\t\n392\t    def teardown(self, keep: bool) -> None:\n393\t        \"\"\"rm -rf home_root unless keep=True or eval failed.\"\"\"\n394\t\n395\t    def state_path(self, suffix: str) -> Path:\n396\t        \"\"\"Resolve {suffix} template — {session_id}, {project_key}, etc.\"\"\"\n397\t```\n398\t\n399\t### Key correctness invariants\n400\t\n401\t1. `HOME` is set *before* spawn; child cannot see test-runner's `~/.claude/`.\n402\t2. Per-eval HOMEs are sibling directories under `home_root` — no two evals share a `HOME`, even at `--parallel 15`.\n403\t3. Teardown is best-effort; failure to `rm -rf` is logged but does not affect eval result.\n404\t4. HomeIsolation — extension of existing `IsolationLayers`\n\n### Existing primitive (read-only — cite for reuse)\n\n`src/superclaude/cli/sprint/executor.py:107-182` `IsolationLayers` already implements 4-layer per-subprocess isolation:\n\n| Layer | Env var | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| Working directory | `CLAUDE_WORK_DIR` | Per-task cwd |\n| Git ceiling | `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` | Prevents accidental parent-repo writes |\n| Plugin dir | `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DIR` | Isolates plugin discovery |\n| Settings dir | `CLAUDE_SETTINGS_DIR` | Isolates `settings.json` per subprocess |\n\n### What we add (new — `cli/eval/isolation.py`)\n\n`HomeIsolation` subclasses or composes `IsolationLayers` and adds:\n\n| Layer | Env var | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| **HOME** | `HOME` (and `XDG_*` overrides) | Per-eval `~/.claude/` — full hook+state+log isolation |\n| **Session ID stamp** | `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` | Deterministic session_id for assertion lookups (eval-id-derived) |\n| **Time offset** | `CLAUDE_FAKE_TIME_OFFSET` | Optional; lets evals advance the clock for 30-min freshness tests (E3) |\n\n### Interface signature (not implementation)\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass HomeIsolation:\n    eval_id: str                   # e.g., \"E1\" or \"E2.1\"\n    home_root: Path                # /tmp/eval-runs/<run>/E1/home\n    session_id: str                # deterministic: hash(eval_id + run_id)[:16]\n    time_offset_sec: int = 0\n\n    def setup(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Create HOME/.claude/{hooks,state,logs}; deploy 9 freshness scripts;\n        write settings.json; seed state files per manifest.\"\"\"\n\n    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:\n        \"\"\"Return env-var overlay for the subprocess: HOME, XDG_*, CLAUDE_*,\n        plus pass-through of PATH, USER, TERM, LANG, CI.\"\"\"\n\n    def teardown(self, keep: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"rm -rf home_root unless keep=True or eval failed.\"\"\"\n\n    def state_path(self, suffix: str) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Resolve {suffix} template — {session_id}, {project_key}, etc.\"\"\"\n```\n\n### Key correctness invariants\n\n1. `HOME` is set *before* spawn; child cannot see test-runner's `~/.claude/`.\n2. Per-eval HOMEs are sibling directories under `home_root` — no two evals share a `HOME`, even at `--parallel 15`.\n3. Teardown is best-effort; failure to `rm -rf` is logged but does not affect eval result.\n4. Failed evals **always** retain HOME for post-mortem (the `keep=True` override).\n5. **Path containment guard (security-critical).** Before any filesystem write, `HomeIsolation.setup()` MUST:\n   - (a) Reject any `eval_id` not matching the loader regex (defense-in-depth — loader already validated, but HomeIsolation re-checks).\n   - (b) Compute `home_path = (home_root / eval_id / \"home\").resolve(strict=False)` AND `scratch_root = home_root.resolve(strict=False)`.\n   - (c) Verify `home_path.is_relative_to(scratch_root)` (Python 3.9+). If False, raise `HomeContainmentViolation` and abort the eval (mark ERRORED, no teardown attempt on the partial dir).\n   - (d) Verify `scratch_root` itself matches one of the allowed prefixes: `/tmp/eval-runs/`, `<repo_root>/.dev/eval-runs/`, or the path passed via `--output-dir` after equivalent resolution + prefix check against an allowlist set in `EvalConfig.allowed_scratch_roots`.\n   - (e) Resolve all symlinks under `home_path` after creation but BEFORE deploying hooks (catches the \"scratch dir is a symlink to `$HOME`\" attack).\n6. **Atomic setup contract.** `HomeIsolation.setup()` is wrapped in try/except; on any exception after `mkdtemp` succeeds, the partial HOME is preserved (status ERRORED, `keep=True` forced) and a `setup_failed` artifact tag is written. Distinguishes harness-side bugs from eval-body failures in the report.\n\n---\n\n## 8. The marginal cost of a ~50 LOC `to_junit()` renderer plus one Click option is small; the marginal benefit (zero-config CI publishing without a separate adapter) is real and is the use case spec §4 example #4 already shows.\n5. **Risk R1 (\"Flag drift between spec §4 and implementation\") is closed by this decision.** §4 table is updated to list `--junit`; FR-CLI1 (R-072) already lists it; implementation already wires it. meminfo.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n    available: Optional[int] = None\n    free: Optional[int] = None\n    for line in text.splitlines():\n        key, tokens:\n            continue\n        try:\n            kb = int(tokens[0])\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n        unit = tokens[1].lower() if len(tokens) > 1 else \"kb\"\n        # /proc/meminfo always reports in kB on Linux; the unit check is\n        # defensive in case a future kernel changes the format.\n        multiplier = 1024 if unit == \"kb\" else 1\n        value = kb * multiplier\n        if key == \"MemAvailable\":\n            available = value\n        elif key == \"MemFree\":\n            free = value\n    if available is not None:\n        return available\n    return free\n\n\ndef _check_free_ram_for_parallel(\n    *,\n    requested_parallel: Optional[int],\n    probe: Optional[Callable[[], Optional[int]]] = None,\n    ceiling_bytes: int = The spec carried conditional language in two non-adjacent places: §9 (\"`junit.xml` ... Generated only when `--junit` is passed\") and §10 (\"Add `to_json()` and `to_junit()` (new methods)\"), while the §4 flag table omitted `--junit` from the 11-flag list. The roadmap FR-CLI1 row (R-072) and the Phase-4 task T04.10 both name a 12-flag set that includes `--junit`. The drift between §4 and FR-CLI1 is the surface OQ-7 was opened to close.\n492\t\n493\tDOC-OQ7 (R-076) names two outcomes: (a) wire `--junit` into FR-CLI1 with `junit.xml` emission, OR (b) remove the conditional `--junit` language from spec §9. Either resolves the drift; the choice is binding for M4 exit.\n494\t\n495\t### Options\n496\t\n497\t| Option | Description | Pros | Cons |\n498\t|---|---|---|---|\n499\t| **A. Wire `--junit` into FR-CLI1.** Add the 12th flag; Reporter's `to_junit()` and `emit_junit` gate stand. Update spec §4 table to list `--junit`. | Matches the existing roadmap FR-CLI1 spec (R-072, 12 flags) and the Phase-4 T04.10 acceptance criterion (\"lists all 12 flags named in FR-CLI1\"). Reuses already-landed `to_junit()` (~50 LOC) without code removal. Keeps CI consumers' future path (JUnit-XML ingestion in CI runners is the de-facto pattern for pytest-style harnesses). | Adds one CLI flag and one feature-gated output file. |\n500\t| B. Remove `--junit` from spec §9 and `to_junit()` from §10. | Slightly smaller CLI surface; one fewer artifact path. | Contradicts the roadmap row R-072 (which would also need amendment), invalidates T04.10's \"12 flags\" AC (would need to be re-spun as \"11 flags\"), and forces re-removal of Reporter code that has already landed under T03.13. The cost is documentation churn in 3 places plus code deletion for net-zero capability change. |\n501\t\n502\t### Decision: **A — wire `--junit` into FR-CLI1; spec §9 conditional language is correct as written; spec §4 flag table updated to include `--junit` for consistency.**\n503\t\n504\t### Rationale\n505\t\n506\t1. **The implementation has already converged on option A.** The Reporter's `to_junit()` method and `emit_junit` constructor flag landed under T03.13 (`src/superclaude/cli/eval/reporter.py:146,177,222-225`); the CLI's `--junit` flag landed under T04.10 (`src/superclaude/cli/eval/commands.py:1349-1352,1366,1593`). Choosing option B now would require deleting working code to match a spec that no other artifact endorses.\n507\t2. **The roadmap and tasklist already commit to 12 flags.** R-072 acceptance criterion enumerates 12 flag names including `--junit`; T04.10 acceptance criterion says \"all 12 flags named in FR-CLI1\". Option B would require amending both, plus removing the `to_junit()` line from spec §10 and the §9 junit.xml section.
